title: throughput-regression-continuous-batching-debug-scratchpad-8
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad capturing commands, logs, hypotheses while tracking the recent throughput regression affecting continuous batching on staging/dedicated clusters. Not a polished incident report — notes to self and collaborators.

Synopsis:
- Regression surfaced 2026-01-14 after deploy of batching refactor (PR 482).
- Observed ~25-40% drop in tokens/sec on 2x worst-case routes (seq_len 1024, bursty short requests).
- Latency P95 increased ~30-40ms and tail behaviour worsened.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-01-14 03:10 UTC: Deployment of batching refactor (feature flag: continuous-batching-v2).
- 2026-01-14 03:45 UTC: Alerts for throughput drop and SLO violations.
- 2026-01-14 04:10 UTC: Rollback to continuous-batching-v1, partial improvement.
- 2026-01-15 -> ongoing: Re-enable on canary nodes to reproduce.

What I reproduced locally:
- Repro script: python tools/load_test.py --qps 200 --seq 1024 --model rwd-llama-13b --duration 10m
- With continuous-batching-v2 enabled: tokens/sec ~ 125k
- With v1 (old batching): tokens/sec ~ 170k

Commands I ran:
- kubectl -n staging get pods -l app=inference -o wide
- kubectl logs -f deployment/inference --since=1h | grep "batch" | tail -n 200
- curl -s -X POST "http://staging-infer/api/v1/streams" -d '{"input": "test"}' | jq .
- python -m tools/bench/compare --config configs/continuous-batching-v2.yaml
- docker exec -it runtime-node bash -c "ps aux | grep inference_worker"
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,utilization.memory --format=csv -l 5

Prometheus / Metrics queries I used:
- avg(rate(tokens_generated_total[1m])) by (model)
- sum(rate(requests_total{route="/v1/generate"}[1m])) by (pod)
- histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le,route))
- Observed that tokens_generated_total per GPU dropped roughly in line with tokens/sec from the bench.

Key log excerpts (simplified):
- "INFO continuous_batcher: assembled batch size=6 latency_ms=12 kv_cache_hit=false"
- "WARN batching_scheduler: flush_timer expired code=forced_flush reason=idle_timeout
  worker_queue_len=3 pending_batches=1"
- "ERROR runtime_executor: failed to merge kv cache segment id=0 size=0 expected>0
  trace_id=abc123"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Unexpected forced flush/idle timeout behavior in v2 batching scheduler causing smaller-than-expected batches in bursty traffic. (Most likely)
2) KV-cache merging bug (see ERROR above) causing per-request extra overhead or retries.
3) Kernel selection path change in v2 leads to non-optimal CUDA kernels for some sequence-length combos.
4) Telemetry aggregation bug makes tokens/sec look lower (less likely — metrics verified on host-level counters).

Evidence supporting (1):
- Logs show many forced_flush events during bursty windows.
- Canary when run with artificially steady traffic (no bursts) achieves similar throughput to v1.

Evidence supporting (2):
- ERROR runtime_executor: failed to merge kv cache segment — reproduces occasionally under high concurrency.
- When I disabled kv_cache merging (dev flag: KV_CACHE_MERGE=false) throughput improved ~8% but not full delta.

Quick tests and results:
- Toggle continuous-batching-v2 on single canary pod -> throughput down 30% on that pod.
- Set KV_CACHE_MERGE=false on canary + v2 -> throughput down only 20% (improved).
- Increase batch_window_ms from 5 -> 12 (v2) -> batch sizes increased from median 4 -> median 7 and tokens/sec improved ~12%.

Temporary mitigations tried:
- Rollback to v1 (rolled to 50% of fleet) -> customer impact reduced but wanted root cause.
- Increase batch_window_ms on v2 to allow slightly longer batching; helped but increases tail latency.
- Disable KV cache merging (not safe long-term).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Why does v2's scheduler trigger forced_flush more aggressively? Check new heuristics in PR 482 (look at flush_threshold logic).
- Inspect PR 482 diff for changes around time-based flush vs size-based flush.
- Replicate ERROR around kv cache merging with deterministic repro (need a replay harness for concurrent requests).
- Check CUDA kernel selection logs (enable runtime.DEBUG=kernel_selector) on canary and compare kernel ids between v1 and v2.
- Add finer-grained tracing around flush_timer events and record batch size distribution per flush.

Notes / snippets for follow-up commands:
- Grep for flush logic: git --no-pager grep -n "flush_timer" -S -- serving-runtime/ | sed -n '1,120p'
- Run bench with csv output: python tools/load_test.py --qps 200 --seq 1024 --duration 10m --out results/v2-run.csv
- Enable kernel selector debug: kubectl set env deployment/inference RUNTIME_DEBUG=kernel_selector --namespace=staging --record
- Reproduce kv-merge error: python tools/repro/kv_merge_race.py --concurrency 128 --seq 512 --duration 5m

Notes-to-self (style):
- Keep this doc rough. Capture timestamps and any new commands here.
- After root cause narrowed, convert into clean postmortem draft in confluence.

Last manual snapshot:
- 2026-01-26 11:33 UTC: Ran long-run 1h ramp test with v2 + batch_window_ms=12 -> tokens/sec still 8% below v1 baseline (so changes help but not full fix).

Next immediate step (today):
- Add extra logging around forced_flush reason and worker_queue_len for one canary node; collect 30m of data during peak.
- Pair with Lina to step through PR 482 heuristics.

References:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/482
- JIRA: JIRA-RI-1297 (internal)

-- Asha
